We adopt probability calibration (temperature scaling) on Stage~2 prior to threshold selection when transferring thresholds across datasets, following \cite{guo2017calibration}; under distribution shift, calibration effects can vary and should be reported with care \cite{minderer2021revisiting}.

\subsection{Cross-Dataset Evaluation (Deepfake-Eval-2024)}
% The Deepfake-Eval-2024 calibrated and Stage2-only tables are included in the auto tables above.

On Deepfake\hyp Eval\hyp 2024, the calibrated cascade exhibits substantially lower absolute performance than in\hyp distribution validation (Table~\ref{tab:deepeval_calibrated}). This gap is expected given the distribution shift, variety of sources, and lack of fine\hyp tuning on the OOD corpus. A Stage~2\,only setting (Table~\ref{tab:deepeval_stage2only}) shows the upper bound when the expert handles nearly all samples, at the cost of high system load. These results motivate domain adaptation or dataset\hyp aware calibration for deployment.

\subsection{Routing Strategies: Confidence vs. Entropy vs. Margin}
We compare confidence\hyp based routing (ours) with entropy and margin alternatives \cite{kaya2019shallowdeep,teerapittayanon2017branchynet}. Confidence routing offers direct control of the escalation rate via $(\tau_{\mathrm{low}},\tau_{\mathrm{high}})$ and pairs well with calibration; entropy and margin can be emulated within the same framework. A summary table is provided as a template for future runs.

\subsection{Robustness to Common Perturbations}
We evaluate the tuned cascade under four perturbation families (JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, motion blur, and brightness/contrast). Figure~\ref{fig:robustness_curves} plots F1 vs. perturbation strength (additional Accuracy and FNR plots are provided in the repository). Results exhibit non\hyp monotonic trends across families:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{JPEG:} F1 mildly improves as quality decreases (95\,$\rightarrow$\,20), accompanied by a reduction in FNR. This likely reflects compression artifacts that accentuate cues learned by the detector; full-sample evaluation is needed to confirm.
  \item \textbf{Gaussian:} Increasing noise (sigma 2\,$\rightarrow$\,12) lowers FNR and raises F1 in the small-sample sweep. We hypothesize that heavy noise disrupts real textures more than fake cues under the current thresholds; a larger run and per-family calibration will clarify.
  \item \textbf{Motion blur:} F1 improves from kernel 3 to 13 with a gradual drop in FNR, indicating partial robustness to blur at the tested sizes.
  \item \textbf{Brightness:} Moderate brightness changes (0.7\,$\rightarrow$\,1.3) show a slight F1 increase and FNR decrease.
\end{itemize}
These results motivate per\hyp family threshold/temperature calibration and consistent reporting of Stage\-2 escalation rates to quantify efficiency\hyp robustness trade\hyp offs. Prior analyses suggest frequency artifacts from generative up\hyp sampling are informative \cite{durall2020watch}, and adaptive frequency filtering or blending cues (Face X\-Ray) can be beneficial \cite{qian2020thinkingfrequency,li2020facexray}. JPEG/noise may accentuate some cues at certain thresholds; a per\hyp family calibration protocol is therefore appropriate. We note that, beyond natural perturbations, adversarial attacks (e.g., CW, PGD) can severely degrade detector performance if unaccounted for \cite{carlini2017towards,madry2018towards}; reporting calibrated thresholds and escalation rates helps bound risk under operational budgets. Table~\ref{tab:robustness_table} summarizes F1/Acc/FNR/S2 Rate by perturbation and level. We further sweep thresholds to visualize FNR vs. Stage~2 rate; Figure~\ref{fig:robustness_tradeoff} shows representative trade\hyp offs.

\paragraph{Temporal segmentation and partial forgeries.} Beyond video\hyp level decisions, frame\hyp level segmentation of forged segments has been explored to handle partial manipulations \cite{undercover2023}. Our two\hyp stage architecture is compatible with such post\hyp processing: Stage~1 can pre\hyp filter frames and Stage~2 can refine segment boundaries under a budget.
